newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance modestly in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance modestly in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rose modestly in early morning trading on Thursday on the back of positive corporate earnings news and the good performance of overseas markets, brokers said.
However, the market's near-term outlook remained cloudy, they added.
"The market must test 11,300 or drop back, said Priscilla Ng, executive director at CEF GC Brokerage Ltd.
The Hang Seng Index gained 39 points in the first 30 minutes of trade to 11,281.71. Turnover was moderate at HK$735 million.
Ng said the earnings' results of the Henderson Land group, which were released Wednesday evening, were good but generally in line with market expectations.

Some brokers, however, were more upbeat, pointing out that Hong Kong investors, like thosein the United States, had already discounted a small hike in U.S. and Hong Kong interest rates and remained overweighted in the Hong Kong market.
"Hong Kong investors are still actively seeking blue chips," said K.L.Wong, institutional sales manager at Kerry Securities Ltd. He added the Henderson group results were positive for the market.
Property shares led the market with the sub-index up 0.29 percent after 45 minutes of trade, compared with the Hang Seng's 0.13 percent gain.
Henderson Land, whose 19 percent increase in 1996 earnings was just slightly better than market expectation gained, HK$0.25 to HK$61.25.

Subsidiary Henderson Investment, which reported a disappointing 16 percent rise in 1996 after-tax profits, was marked down HK$0.20 to HK$7.95, but Henderson China rose HK$0.35 to HK$17.35 on strong results..
"Both Henderson Land and Henderson China look positive, but we have downgraded Henderson Investment," said Kerry's Wong.e

HSBC also gained HK$0.50 in morning trading to HK$135.00. The share, along with Henderson Land, has been leading the market since March, said technical analysts. Bank of East Asia gained HK$0.10 to HK$27.75.Property shares led the market with the sub-index up 0.29 percent after 45 minutes of trade, compared with the Hang Seng's 0.13 percent gain.

Among the most active were CNPC (Hong Kong) which rose HK$0.015 to HK$0.365. The company, which is China-backed and involved in oil and gas exploration, recently announced the placement of 33.1 million shares with a Canadian investment company. The funds raised will be used to repay the company's debts.
